title: Augustine's doubt on the heavens; Greeks and Latins before him affirm corruption of the heavens

pass_b_english: Augustine dissents (City of God book 20, chapter 24), and speaking doubtfully on Psalm 101: There are, he says, three heavens of heavens superior in the firmament. But whether they themselves also will perish by fire, or only those heavens which also perished in the flood, is a somewhat more scrupulous debate among the learned; nor can it easily be explained, especially in the narrowness of time. But how many now follow Augustine's sentence, Sixtus of Siena shows (Sacred Library book 6, annotation 246) and Feuardentius on Irenaeus book 4, chapter 6.

Against whom you will set the fathers, both all the Greeks and the Latins who wrote before Augustine — namely Justin Martyr, or whoever else, in the Confutation of Aristotle's Dogmas book 2 On the Heavens denying that the heavens can be corrupted; Irenaeus book 4, chapter 6; Ambrose Hexaemeron book 1, chapter 6; and among juniors also Augustinus Eugubinus on 2 Peter 3; and Hieronymus Magius On the Burning of the World book 2, chapters 6 and 7.
source_text: Dissentit Augustinus lib. 20. de C.D. cap. 24. & dubie loquens in psal. 101. Sunt, inquit, tres caeli caelorum superiores in firmamento. Sed utrum & ipsi perituri sint igni, an hi soli caeli qui etiam diluvio perierunt, disceptatio est aliquanto scrupulosior inter doctos; nec facile, maxime in angustia temporis, explicari potest. Quam multi vero nunc Augustini sequantur sententiam, Sixtus Senensis ostendit lib. 6. bibl. sanct. annot. 246. & Feuardentius in Irenaeum lib. 4. cap. 6. Quibus oppones patres tum Graecos universos, tum Latinos, qui ante Augustinum scripserunt, nominatim Justinum Martyrem, sive quemcunque alium in confut. dogm. Aristotelis lib. 2. de caelo neganti caelos posse corrumpi, Irenaeum lib. 4. cap. 6. Ambrosium lib. 1. Hexaem. cap. 6. & e junioribusque Augustinum Eugubinum in 2.Pet. 3. & Hieronymum Magium lib. 2. de exustione mundi cap. 6. & 7.
